method: Static reverse engineering only; no specimen code executed. Read RULES.md and TAXONOMY.md. Used atomscan --no-update --mode slow --follow=none, cleave facts, Rizin, manual script decoding, UPX unpacking and osslsigncode.

samples.identification: Shipping-document lure containing a registry-cached PowerShell download-to-shellcode loader; Remcos attribution remains unconfirmed.
execution_trace: Unami starts at one-based character 11, keeps one character every five, and stops 12 characters before the end. Nationhoods = Asc(")") - 40 = 1. Junk functions and unrelated arithmetic obscure the active path.

Decoded assignments set process environment Semihumanitarian to the concatenated PowerShell and ensnarled to a quoted PowerShell executable path. RegRead tests WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\ProgramFilesDir to select SysWOW64 versus System32 PowerShell.

The reconstructed WScript.Shell.Run command is cmd.exe /v:on /c echo ^%Semihumanitarian^% | !ensnarled! - ; Run uses window style zero. Three Execute statements evaluate the environment assignments and the Run statement.

The numeric key spells Asexualisation. Subtraction decodes iex, [Convert]::FromBase64String, a cyclic byte-XOR expression, and a character-array join. Base64 then cyclic XOR decodes the remaining commands.

Msxml2.ServerXMLHTTP.6.0 performs synchronous GET to https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1ZMsbOxJJHJaNpGyhIw2DqweS6fGG0SOm with a Firefox user agent. Successful response text is stored as declaratorily under HKCU:\Seksten\Gennembruds. Existing cache data can skip the download loop.
The cache is Base64-decoded and converted to ASCII; substring(167602,33890) is evaluated through the reconstructed iex.

Forager recovered the current Google Drive response (268656 bytes; provenance retained in scratch). The decoded stage uses Reflection.Emit to build P/Invoke signatures, hides its window with ShowWindow, reconstructs an environment block, and allocates an executable buffer with VirtualAlloc protection 64.

Marshal.Copy copies the first 16514 decoded bytes into executable memory and the next 151088 bytes to a second allocation. CallWindowProcA transfers execution to the first buffer with the second buffer and NtProtectVirtualMemory address as arguments. This is a native shellcode launch, not document processing.
samples.judgment_reason: Concealed remote acquisition, registry payload caching, hidden interpreter launch and executable-memory handoff outweigh a hypothetical legitimate document workflow. No deployment authorization or final RAT configuration is available. Current fetched content is supplemental evidence; the supplied VBS itself already establishes concealed remote-code execution.
samples.coverage: Two suspicious reconstruction/evaluation findings plus all original neutral operations are retained. Static manual decoding proves hostility, but these generic raw-source predicates do not justify hostile execution claims. Full stride/subtraction/XOR decoding is not performed by the detector, leaving downstream network/cache/shellcode behavior undetected on the original VBS.
samples.coverage_gap: The two suspicious findings satisfy the fallback coverage bar. Do not invent a Remcos identity or duplicate generic constituents as hostile rules.
samples.external_sources: Bazaar and Triage could not be opened through the web tool. No family claim is inferred from their labels.
samples.marker_line: Shipping VBS: hidden download-to-shellcode; correct overclaims

samples.identification: zzhelloworld_socktest RubyGem 0.1.9, claimed author derekiops, description test gem do not use.
execution_trace: lib/zzhelloworld_socktest.rb is plain Ruby. Requiring it evaluates the module body immediately, connects TCPSocket.new to 66.78.40.218:32768, reopens STDIN/STDOUT/STDERR onto the same socket, then execs /bin/sh -i.
The execution is at require time, not a gem-install lifecycle hook. There is no opt-in wrapper, local-only test boundary, caller-selected endpoint or authentication.
README contains a mostly inert HTML security-parser corpus and generated gem boilerplate. The SVG calls alert(0x539). These files do not constrain or explain away the Ruby reverse-shell path.
The version file confirms 0.1.9. The malicious code is first-party package content, not a fetched dependency.
samples.judgment_reason: Research-test branding is plausible, but an automatic interactive shell to a fixed public host is an unbounded backdoor when this library is loaded. No authorization or controlled deployment is supplied.
samples.coverage: The existing hostile ruby-reopened-stdio-shell finding is unchanged on the Ruby file, data.tar.gz and gem. All socket, descriptor and process primitives remain.
samples.coverage_gap: Only one distinct hostile behavior is supported: the reverse shell. A second hostile rule would duplicate it. No stealing, persistence or other objective is invented to meet a numeric minimum.
samples.corroboration: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-86pf-258h-xmh8 independently describes the same require-time endpoint, stream redirection and shell.
samples.marker_line: Socktest 0.1.9: require-time reverse shell; retain precise detection

samples.identification: Unsigned native Windows overlay dropper with a UPX-packed wideshut.exe rootkit/service loader, a copy/launch helper and a bundled ADB executable. Omnibus collector filename is not a family identification.
execution_trace: The outer program enters the staging routine at 0x402300. It reads its own overlay and builds random executable paths under TEMP, using TEMP\Low when the integrity-level check returns 0x1000. 0x4020b0 writes an extracted image and copies timestamps. ShellExecuteExW at 0x40279a launches another staged image with quoted arguments. The later CreateProcessW at 0x4028f9 uses STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW with show zero.

The 65536-byte helper at outer offset 0x12818 accepts command-line paths, copies files with CopyFileW in a retry loop, invokes ShellExecuteExW at 0x401301, then deletes a supplied file. The helper is not itself a proven credential stealer.
wideshut.exe begins at outer offset 0x1f630. UPX decompresses it to 2470912 bytes. Its main at 0x402b40 chooses install paths based on token/elevation and command-line modes.

Its embedded native programs replace their MZ bytes with FFFF. Writer 0x4030a0 restores M and Z at 0x4030b6/0x4030bc, creates the output, writes the buffer at 0x4031c0, and can copy times from System32\himem.sys with GetFileTime and SetFileTime.
The install path at 0x4021f0 writes System32\drivers\hfile.sys, creates and starts a kernel-driver service, and writes embedded DLL bytes to System32\msfte.dll and System32\oci.dll.

After writing msfte.dll it restarts WSearch. After writing oci.dll, it stops MSDTC, executes cmd.exe /c sc config msdtc obj= LocalSystem through CreateProcessW at 0x4026ac, waits, then restarts MSDTC at 0x4026e4.
0x401da0 writes/starts bindsvc.exe and passes a process selection string through IOCTL 0x222004. Wrapper 0x401c10 opens \\.\HideDriver; 0x401bc0 calls DeviceIoControl at 0x401c01.

The embedded driver at unpacked raw offset 0x26800 has a valid PE except for its replaced MZ bytes. A separate analysis copy restores only those bytes. The driver imports KeServiceDescriptorTable, contains file/process-hider implementations, registers a device/control interface and has hook-management code. The loader operationally supplies process-hide rules; this is not merely a rootkit-related string in an unrelated program.

The ROR13 constants were verified against the embedded resolver code: ror eax,13 followed by character addition and comparisons against LoadLibraryA/GetProcAddress hashes. They are real resolver instructions here.

The embedded DocxToText helper is readable source that extracts document.xml, writes text and deletes the source DOCX. Its name and Function/End Function markers are not obfuscation. Its presence does not establish actual document theft or observed execution.

The separate ADB image has normal Android Debug Bridge command/help strings and a Quick Heal certificate blob. Cleave marks the signature unverified; osslsigncode rejects verification because the embedded certificate is not at EOF in the carved image. No valid signature chain or malicious ADB behavior is asserted. The outer file is unsigned; legitimate bundled tools do not neutralize the traced service/driver actions.
samples.judgment_reason: Concealed native payload restoration, service-DLL replacement with LocalSystem reconfiguration, rootkit control, hidden launch and timestamp copying support malicious deployment. No legitimate installer UI, publisher authorization or deployment context explains these paths. Runtime success and actor/family attribution remain unproven.
samples.coverage: Two new hostile findings cover header-restoring hashed-API file staging and MSDTC/OCI service-loader replacement on wideshut.exe and its UPX layer. Existing API-hashing and unsigned-Microsoft-resource observations remain. Neutral Low-path, filename, embedded-VB and API conjunctions remain visible under accurate homes.
samples.coverage_gap: The outer file retains a suspicious opaque-overlay finding and all capability observations; the hostile findings reside in the embedded/UPX stages. Automatic extraction misses MZ-erased nested images. Driver rule dispatch, timestamp-copy data flow and WSearch DLL replacement are manually established but do not yet have independent generalizable hostile detections.
samples.marker_line: Native stager: concealed PEs and service DLL hijack; improve coverage

unsupported_claims_and_corrections: junk-padded-vbs-powershell-execute-stage required only concatenation, numeric-array text, WScript.Shell and Execute. It proved neither hidden PowerShell nor a linked launch. It falsely convicted the checked-in fragmented-array-eval control. Consolidated into the existing suspicious fragmented-PowerShell/evaluation observation; every constituent remains.

vbs-stride-decoded-execute-stage inferred a decoded-stage launch from Mid-near-arithmetic, Execute and WScript.Shell. Retained its exact match population as suspicious and merged it with the existing stride/concatenation/evaluation predicate: shared Mid and eval, with either WSH or concatenation corroboration. This union preserves both prior conjunctions.

ruby-reverse-shell could fire on a socket connection beside STDIN.reopen without any shell or socket-to-shell binding. Retired that unsupported backdoor inference. Socket, stream and process findings remain, and the unchanged fd-redirect rule retains the proven attack. No count or classifier target justifies this correction.
A Low-directory executable path establishes neither TEMP nor staging/masquerade. Moved the unchanged matcher and exclusions to fs/path/reference with a precise reference description.
Search(System|User|Admin)Host.exe text proves a filename reference, not that a payload uses it. Moved it unchanged to fs/path/basename.

Embedded PEs, a Low path, a host-like name and WriteFile do not bind a dropped image or its filename. Likewise ShellExecuteEx/DeleteFile/snapshot imports beside a Low string do not bind a launched payload. Moved both unchanged conjunctions to notable file-write and shell-launch API profiles; removed unsupported attack mappings.

Eight-character procedure names and End Function do not prove an obfuscated script. DocxToText is a concrete ordinary match. Moved this unchanged source-shape predicate and exclusions to notable metadata; updated every exact consumer and removed unsupported obfuscation wording from the two WSH consumer descriptions.
rule_review.new_detection_design: New atoms describe an actual same-buffer MZ-store instruction sequence, the OCI DLL reference, and the MSDTC LocalSystem command. New hostile composites require content-derived payload reconstruction plus file/launch or service-loader context. No collector filename, C2 IOC, exact sample size or sample exception gates them.
rule_review.placement: Five matcher/scope-preserving moves verified against a git-archive baseline. All rules are in existing leaf directories admitted by the validator. Low has no required TEMP prefix, so fs/path/reference is the supported path subject; executable-name text is fs/path/basename. New payload activation is execution/payload/file-exec; service reactivation is persistence/system/service/loader.
rule_review.consumers: Searched exact and ancestor references before editing. All exact embedded-VB consumers and fixture assertions were updated. The broader Ruby backdoor selectors have no consumer relying on its broad co-occurrence rule. Shared rules were not weakened on verdict, queue or classifier grounds.

verification.original_scans: atomscan and cleave facts run on every original. Before/after reports include all archive members and UPX layers; stored in evidence_directory.
verification.vbs_controls: Seven existing ordinary-evaluation/reconstruction/registry controls pass. The former hostile predicates matched ordinary controls before correction. The new stride predicate preserves the union of prior reconstruction conjunctions.
verification.external_positive: Forager fetched sha256 0d155cbaa50ce44c1c38e3a37f890bae30fc2271d88d91504dc2e7c835e50795 as AALPDA.vbe with provenance. Its previously reviewed registry-staged concealed downloader uses the same stride technique. After ID mapping/consolidation, zero observation losses.
verification.ruby_controls: Six existing parsed-source controls pass, retaining actual descriptor-shell attacks and excluding quoted/commented examples and unrelated streams.
verification.native_controls: Four feature-removal controls use the actual unpacked payload: original matches both new hostile rules; changing the MZ-write byte removes both; changing OCI or the MSDTC command removes only service-loader detection. No specimen executes.
verification.other_fixtures: Existing inert temp-low mimic, normal temp staging tool and Elex LPADV positive profile fixture retain identical observations after documented ID mapping. The Elex fixture is synthetic matcher coverage, not a claimed real malware execution.
verification.material_detection_losses: Intentional: VBS loses two unsupported hostile classifications while retaining two suspicious concealment observations; gem loses one unsupported suspicious co-occurrence classification while retaining the actual hostile reverse shell; native broad drop/launch/obfuscated-helper claims become accurate neutral observations. All unchanged attack detections and low-level observations are retained; two new native hostile behaviors are detected. No unexpected member-level observation losses.
verification.classifier_disagreement: The shipping RAR loses its calibrated alert (level 0 to -1) after correcting overclaims, even though aggregate probability remains 0.99945. This is a classifier miss, not grounds to restore false traits. The VBS and Ruby malicious members remain ML misses. The packed wideshut wrapper remains ML-negative, while its UPX output now alerts. Gem and native outer alert levels remain 1 and 25.
verification.limitations: The README analysis reports flow-graph-limited; this does not affect the plain Ruby reverse-shell path. Model bundle warns that its v18 feature spec predates extractor v19. No runtime execution, operator authorization or final Remcos payload was established.
verification.final_check: Required final action: make validate. Its result is reported in the final response; no inline YARA source was changed.
